en.question: What does HTTP, at the start of web addresses, stand for?
en.fact: Tim Berners-Lee created it at CERN around 1990, along with HTML and the first web browser.

es.question: ¿Qué significa HTTP, la sigla al principio de las direcciones web?
options: Proceso de texto de alta transferencia
Programa de transporte de texto con hipervínculos
Protocolo de transferencia de terminal doméstica
es.fact: Lo creó Tim Berners-Lee en el CERN alrededor de 1990, junto con el HTML y el primer navegador web.

en.question: Who co-founded Microsoft with Paul Allen?
en.fact: They started it in 1975. The name is short for "microcomputer software".

en.question: Which company makes the PlayStation?
en.fact: It grew out of a cancelled project with Nintendo to build a CD add-on for the Super Nintendo.

en.question: What does the "e" in "email" stand for?
en.fact: Ray Tomlinson sent the first network email in 1971 and chose the @ sign to separate the user's name from the computer's.

en.question: What does USB stand for?
en.fact: USB first came out in 1996. USB-C, which plugs in either way up, arrived in 2014.

en.question: In what year was the first iPhone released?
en.fact: Steve Jobs introduced it as "an iPod, a phone and an internet communicator" in one device.

en.question: What was the very first .com domain ever registered?
en.fact: It was registered on 15 March 1985 by Symbolics, a computer company in Massachusetts.
